text:
The Ducks were down two goals in Calgary by the end of the first period, and they still won their fourth straight. Cutter Gauthier's slap shot with 1:34 left in the third put Anaheim ahead for good, and Nikita Nesterenko added an empty-netter-style insurance goal 20 seconds before the horn to make it 5-3. Gauthier's winner came on a 2% chance by our numbers, the least likely goal of the night, which fits a game that turned on timing more than quality.

The Flames led 3-1 after 20 minutes on goals from William Stromgren, Joel Hanley and a late power-play snap from Joel Farabee, and they had the better of the chances in that period. After that, it was close to one-way traffic. Anaheim out-chanced Calgary in expected goals (the quality of shots taken) 1.28 to 0.58 in the second and 1.56 to 0.42 in the third, and finished with 65 shot attempts to 47. Our simulation of every shot says the Ducks deserved to win about 60% of the time. Tristan Luneau cut the lead in the second, and Leo Carlsson tied it 55 seconds into the third on the power play. Carlsson, the No. 2 pick in 2023, was on the ice for 2.26 expected goals for and just 0.24 against. Beckett Sennecke, drafted third overall in 2024, had two assists and was named first star.

The goaltending shifted the game too. Lukas Dostal allowed three goals on 11 shots before Ville Husso stopped all 10 he faced in relief. For Calgary, Dustin Wolf gave up four on 28 shots, a bit worse than the chances against him called for. The Ducks now have four wins in a row and have split the season series with the Flames at two games each, while Calgary lets a three-goal first period slip away.
